data.name: Ezekion
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name עֶזְקִיאָה (Ezqiyah), meaning 'God will strengthen'. This name is derived from the Hebrew root עזק (azq), meaning 'to be strong'. In the Old Testament, Ezekiel was a prophet who wrote the Book of Ezekiel. He was taken into exile in Babylon and had visions of God's glory.
data.spiritual_meaning: A strong name with divine origin.
data.numerology_meaning: A leader, a trailblazer, and a pioneer.

in_hebrew.name: עזיקיון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עזיקיון הוא שם שמשמעותו 'עוזרו של אלוהים' או 'חזקיהו אלוהים'. השם נגזר מהשורשים העבריים 'עזק' ו'אלוהים', ומציין את התלות והחיבור לאלוהים. השם קשור לנושאים של חוזק וקשר רוחני.

in_greek.name: Εζηκιων
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι η δύναμή μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το Εζηκιων προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές ρίζες και σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι η δύναμή μου' ή 'Εδωκεν ο Θεός δύναμις'. Το όνομα αντανακλά την σχέση με το Θείο και τη πίστη στην θρησκεία.

in_latin.name: Ezekion
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ezekion significat 'Deus est fortitudo mea' vel 'Deus donavit fortitudinem'. Nomen hoc origine hebraica, in traditione christiana, significat fiduciam et robur spiritualem.

in_english.name: Ezekion
in_english.meaning: God is my strength or God strengthens
in_english.long_meaning: Ezekion originates from Hebrew roots, signifying 'God is my strength' or 'God strengthens'. The name conveys a deep spiritual connection, emphasizing reliance on divine power. Historically, names with similar roots are found in biblical contexts, symbolizing faith and resilience. In Christian tradition, Ezekion represents a strong, faith-driven personality.

data.cultural_impact: Ezekiel was a prominent Jewish prophet whose name has been handed down through generations, influencing Jewish and Christian cultures. The Book of Ezekiel is one of the major prophetic books in the Old Testament and has shaped the religious and cultural traditions of the Jewish people and those of the Christian faith. The book's symbolic visions and prophecies, including the famous Vision of the Dry Bones, have been interpreted and retold through various artistic and literary expressions, such as art, music, and literature. These interpretations and retellings have contributed to the richness and diversity of Jewish and Christian cultural traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Ezekiel, meaning 'God will strengthen', conveys a deep spiritual significance. The name reminds us that, as believers, we do not face our trials and challenges alone. Just as God strengthened Ezekiel in his time of exile and helped him deliver His message, God is always with us, providing strength and support in our own times of need. The name Ezekiel reminds us of the promise that, no matter the circumstances, God will continue to strengthen and uphold us.

historical_references.reference: Ezekiel the Syrian, also known as Ezechias or Ezechiel, was a prominent Christian theologian and philosopher of the 5th century AD. He is known for his influential works 'On the Soul' and 'On God', which greatly impacted Neoplatonist and early Christian thought. His philosophical and theological ideas were a bridge between the Hellenistic and Christian traditions.
historical_references.context: Ezechiel was born in Nisibis, in the Roman Empire, and studied under Proclus in Athens. He later founded a monastery in the Syrian desert, where he wrote his influential works. His ideas were influential in the development of Christian Neoplatonism and early Christian philosophy.

historical_references.reference: Ezekiel of Judea, also known as Ezekiel the Priest or Ezekiel the Seer, was a Hebrew prophet mentioned in the Old Testament book of Ezekiel. He is believed to have lived around the 6th century BC during the Babylonian exile. Ezekiel's visions and prophecies provided guidance and hope to the Jewish people during their time of captivity in Babylon and were considered a significant contribution to Jewish and Christian prophetic literature.
historical_references.context: Ezekiel was a priest before the exile and was taken to Babylon along with other Jewish exiles. While in Babylon, he received visions and prophecies from God, which he wrote down and recorded in the book of Ezekiel. His prophecies included promises of restoration and return to Jerusalem, as well as warnings of judgment for disobedience.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Ezekiel, derived from the Hebrew words 'ezek' (strength) and 'kel' (God), has gained modern popularity beyond its biblical context. In fantasy literature, Ezekion is a common variant of the name, appearing in various works as a powerful hero or villain. In tabletop games, it is a popular choice for character names, often associated with strength and divine power. In video games, Ezekion is the name of various characters and locations, reflecting the influence of the biblical name on modern culture.

name_in_real_life.story: Michael Ezekion, a minister in Jerusalem, Israel, shares that their name Ezekion meaning "God will strengthen" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Ezekiel: God’s strength and God’s stone, signifying one who is deeply rooted in divine power and strength to carry out God’s commands.
